subject: Request: Path Economics Explorer + lightweight forensics tile
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Cc: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai, ops@luma.com
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: Path Economics Explorer + lightweight forensics tile

Hi team,

High-level ask: customers (and our CS team) keep asking for a single-pane view that makes it trivial to answer "which API path caused the spend/latency spike?" — right now we stitch together token waterfalls, traces, and ad-hoc queries which is slow and error-prone.

Proposed MVP (what I'd like to scope for the next sprint):
- A console explorer called "Path Economics" that shows per-API-path (endpoint) cost and latency over time, with tenant-scoped filters.
- Quick forensics tile inside each row: one-click drill that shows 1) top caller tenants, 2) p50/p95/p99 latency, 3) token-cost breakdown, 4) link to a lightweight replay URL (export of the trace/sampled inputs).
- Sampling control toggle and expected cost impact estimate when enabling higher-resolution traces for a path.

Why this matters: Skylark Health had repeated spikes last quarter where the root cause was a new prompt format that increased token churn on a particular POST /v1/complete path. CS needed a quick export to show the customer impact.

I attached a rough mockup and a sample csv with the query I used to stitch current data together.

Critical constraints / acceptance criteria:
- Tenant-scoped (must be filterable by tenant id)
- Ability to break down cost by token layer (prompt vs completion) and by model variant (e.g., gpt-large/quantized)
- Drill should surface a replay link to paste into support tickets
- Rollout needs a two-week canary with 2-3 customers (Skylark is willing)

Would like engineering input on feasibility and a prioritized backlog item (INF-4321). Can we get an initial feasibility call this week?

Thanks,
Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Head of Product — Console & Observability
Redwood Inference

Attachments: path-econ-mockup-v1.png (image), sample-query-cost-latency.csv (CSV summary of current ad-hoc queries)
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: Path Economics Explorer + lightweight forensics tile

Thanks Naomi — great write-up and clear asks. A few initial questions and constraints from infra/runtime perspective: 

1) Data sources: do you want the explorer powered by our existing usage-aggregates (token-level metering + latency histograms) or do we need a new streaming aggregation pipeline? The CSV suggests you’re stitching from ad-hoc logs today, which we can replicate but it will add load.

2) Retention/rollups: to keep costs reasonable we should plan daily rollups for >30d and retain high-res (per-request) for 7d. That fits current infra but impacts the replay capability.

3) Traffic footprint: for canary we can sample more aggressively (1-5% full traces). For full rollout we’ll expose sampling knobs; need Product to sign off on default sample-rate and an estimate of token cost uplift.

Proposed phased plan:
A) Phase 1 (MVP, 2 wks): daily aggregated table per-path-per-tenant with p50/p95/p99 latency and token-cost columns + basic UI filters.
B) Phase 2 (4 wks): add lightweight forensic tile with sampled replays and top-callers list; replay links stored as short lived S3 objects.
C) Phase 3 (6–8 wks): realtime-ish 1m window view + on-demand deeper replay for canary customers.

If that roadmap sounds right, I’ll open a tech-design doc and estimate dev effort. I also added INF-4321 to Jira and linked it here: https://jira.redwood.local/browse/INF-4321.

—Marcus

Love this. Prioritization notes from Product:

Must-haves for the MVP (what Sales/CS will accept):
- Filter by tenant and by API path/pattern (wildcards, e.g., POST /v1/complete/*)
- p50/p95/p99 latency and cost-per-call columns (token- and model-split)
- A "export replay" action that creates a short-lived replay link and a summarized sample (max 25 calls)
- Ability to compare two time windows (eg: before vs after a deploy)

Nice-to-haves for Phase 2:
- Model/quantization filter and a small estimate of cost delta if you switch quantization profiles
- Top N callers with tenant contact info pulled from CRM (only for admin users)

Acceptance criteria for canary with Skylark Health:
- Two weeks of data, on-boarded with sampling=2% for replay, no customer-facing performance regressions.
- Console tile must generate replay link under 30s for sampled windows.

Open items for engineering:
- Default sample-rate decision (Marcus)
- Storage pattern for replay exports (short-lived signed objects vs in-index blobs)
- Telemetry needed to measure the cost uplift of enabling the tile (Dylan to propose metrics)

I’ll coordinate with Support to pick 2 canary customers (Skylark confirmed below). Planning review on Thursday?

—Jasmine
